data.name: Project RPG Remastered
data.detailed_description:
Storyline:
You wake up and find you have no idea where you are. Worse, you barely remember anything about the recent past. The only thing you're holding on to is your son's voice, crying for you helplessly, and your wife screaming she loves you, but you can't recall what was happening during that time. Ahead of you is a dirt path, so you follow it. You walk right into a village. You look around and inquire if anyone can help you, but no one is interested in assisting unless you have copper to pay them in return. You go and talk to the ammunition dealer, and he makes you a deal. If you can complete a series of risky quests for him, he will pay you for them individually. Along with taking the time to collect copper, and maybe complete some daring quests, you set out on your journey to look for your wife and son.

How far are you willing to push yourself to regain your memories of what happened?

    Features:
  • multiple weapons to choose from
  • free to roam map areas
  • buying, selling and trading with villagers in the marketplace
  • zombies! (a.k.a ghouls) - beware the outer walls of the village
  • quest choices
  • bounties
  • trading cards, badges, backgrounds, emoticons
There are even more exciting features in the game for you to discover! We are also interested to hear what the community would like to see implemented in future updates!

More Info:
Project RPG is mainly an open world role-playing game, but it also consists of many different genres; horror, action, storytelling and mystery. We wanted to ensure the game has a little something for a wide variety of players. The quests, depending on how you choose to play the game, will vary from being guided with help to find your family, to being left to find out where to go on your own, to how much of the game you view before completion. There are many sites for you to explore, for example the ghoul-infested asylum. Also, the bonuses (weapons, unlocked doors, etc.) you receive after the quest, will be determined by the choice of quest and which villager assigned it.

data.short_description: You wake up on a dirt road, holding on to your last memory of your family screaming for help in front of you. Now, with all odds against you, you must complete challenging and dangerous quests to gain help from the villagers of Bartrone. How far are you willing to go to find your wife and son?

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows XP, Vista, 7, 8 or 10
  • Processador: 2.5 Ghz or faster processor (Intel) / 3.5 Ghz or faster processor (AMD)
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: 1 GB RAM / Widescreen
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 1500 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: optional
  • Notas adicionais: These specifications might cause a slow loading time.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows Vista, 7, 8 or 10
  • Processador: 3 Ghz or faster processor (Intel) / 4 Ghz or faster processor (AMD)
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: 1,5 GB RAM / Widescreen
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 1500 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: onboard
  • Notas adicionais: A Solid State Disk is recommended to speed up the loading time.

reviews.review:
Project RPG Remastered is an ambitious independent action RPG that blends open-world exploration, survival mechanics, and mystery into a personal journey driven by loss and forgotten memories. Developed by Acuze Interactives and published by Displacement Studios, the game opens with an emotionally engaging premise as the protagonist awakens with no recollection of his past except fragmented visions of his missing wife and son. This mystery becomes the driving force behind every step of the adventure, encouraging players to piece together both the character's history and the secrets hidden throughout the world. Rather than immediately sending players into battle, the game begins with humble tasks in the village of Bartrone, where trust must be earned through work instead of freely given. This slower introduction helps establish the game's atmosphere while reinforcing the feeling that survival depends on persistence and resourcefulness.

Exploration is one of the game's strongest elements, rewarding players who venture beyond the village into forests, abandoned structures, and dangerous ruins filled with hostile creatures. The world contains multiple areas to investigate, each presenting opportunities to discover quests, gather resources, and encounter increasingly difficult enemies. The abandoned asylum stands out as one of the more memorable locations thanks to its unsettling atmosphere and horror-inspired design. Combat revolves around a selection of weapons and straightforward action mechanics that prioritize accessibility over complexity. While the battles may not offer the depth of larger role-playing titles, they remain enjoyable enough to support the game's emphasis on exploration and progression rather than serving as its only attraction.

Quest design introduces a welcome sense of flexibility by allowing players to make decisions that affect their rewards and future opportunities. Completing different objectives can unlock new equipment, weapons, or previously inaccessible areas, giving each playthrough a degree of variation. Alongside the main storyline, optional bounties and side activities provide additional incentives to leave the main path and interact with the game's world. Trading also plays an important role, as villagers are willing to buy and sell goods that help players prepare for increasingly dangerous expeditions. This combination of quest choices, trading, exploration, and progression creates a gameplay loop that feels rewarding despite the game's relatively modest scale.

Visually, Project RPG Remastered reflects its independent development roots. Character models, animations, and environments lack the refinement found in modern high-budget RPGs, yet the overall presentation succeeds in creating an appropriately lonely and mysterious atmosphere. The environments focus more on functionality than visual spectacle, allowing players to concentrate on exploration instead of graphical effects. Ambient audio and environmental sounds further reinforce the feeling of isolation, while the soundtrack complements the game's darker moments without overwhelming the experience. Although technical limitations are apparent throughout the adventure, the consistent atmosphere helps maintain immersion and supports the narrative's themes of uncertainty and survival.

The game's greatest strength lies in its willingness to combine several gameplay styles into one cohesive adventure. Open-world exploration, role-playing progression, survival mechanics, horror influences, and narrative-driven objectives all contribute to an experience that feels larger than its budget might suggest. Not every feature reaches its full potential, and some mechanics can feel simplistic or rough around the edges, but there is a clear sense of passion behind the project. Players who appreciate independent RPGs and enjoy uncovering mysteries at their own pace will likely find plenty to enjoy, especially if they value exploration over cinematic presentation and polished production values.

Project RPG Remastered may not rival major role-playing releases in terms of technical execution or visual fidelity, but it offers an engaging adventure fueled by curiosity, gradual character progression, and meaningful exploration. Its intriguing storyline, branching quest rewards, open environments, and blend of action and survival mechanics create an experience that stands out among smaller independent RPGs. Those willing to overlook its rough edges will discover a heartfelt game that prioritizes player freedom and atmospheric storytelling over flashy presentation. It is a respectable effort that demonstrates creativity and ambition, making it a worthwhile experience for fans of indie role-playing games.

Rating: 5/10
